pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The Vermont Journeyman Electrician exam is designed to measure the knowledge needed to perform electrical installations under the direction of a master electrician and to supervise an apprentice electrician or electrician’s helper working under the master electrician’s direction. The exam covers a broad range of electrical knowledge, with emphasis on code application, safe installation practices, wiring systems, electrical equipment, and local requirements. The Vermont Journeyman Electrician exam has been listed with 90 questions and a 4-hour time allowance. Subject areas include general electrical theory and principles, wiring and protection, wiring methods and materials, motors and controls, equipment for general use, special occupancies, special equipment, special conditions, and local amendments. Because the exam includes both broad trade knowledge and code-based content, candidates benefit from studying the NEC structure as well as the practical electrical principles behind the questions.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Vermont recognizes the journeyman electrician license for individuals who perform electrical installations under the direction of a master electrician. A licensed journeyman may also supervise an apprentice electrician or electrician’s helper employed by a master electrician under that master electrician’s direction. This makes the journeyman license an important step for electricians who are building professional responsibility, field leadership, and long-term licensing goals. Vermont journeyman electrician candidates should be prepared to document qualifying electrical experience or approved training according to state requirements. The state’s licensing framework includes apprentices, journeyman electricians, master electricians, and specialty electrical classifications. Candidates pursuing the journeyman credential should focus on the requirements that apply specifically to the journeyman electrician license and the exam associated with that classification.

Motors and controls require knowledge of motor circuits, control equipment, protection, and installation requirements. Equipment for general use may involve common electrical equipment encountered in residential, commercial, or industrial work.

Candidates should determine whether they are pursuing a journeyman electrician license, master electrician license, specialty electrical license, or another electrical credential regulated by the state. Candidates should gather the required records before submitting an application. Once the application is submitted, the state licensing authority reviews the candidate’s eligibility. The state regulates electrician licensing, electrical inspections, electrical installations, and electrical safety requirements. Candidates preparing for a Vermont Master Electrician license should follow the state licensing process rather than a local-only license path. pieces.h: Test Information and Study Materials
pieces.t: Effective Vermont Master Electrician exam preparation should include code review, calculation practice, reference navigation, state licensing review, and repeated exposure to exam-style questions. The NEC is detailed, and candidates need to understand how to use it as a working reference. Study time should focus on learning where information is located, how code sections connect, and how to apply the rule to the facts in the question. A strong study routine may include reading one topic, locating related NEC sections, answering practice questions, reviewing missed answers, and returning to the code book to understand the correct reasoning. The 2026 Electrician Calculations Study Guide is important because calculation questions can be challenging under exam pressure.
